{"self_assessment": "**Impact:** I drew the fish on the scratch pad and assigned the strokes, so the table had a shared plan from the first minute. I laid the start and nose and re-laid the lower tail fin. I also bridged the upper fin into the tail junction. At the final check my trace showed about 151 of 205 dominoes falling, with the pale loops in the middle not connected. I can't promise the judge reads it as a fish, but the outline has a body, a forked tail and a nose, and the main run is connected. One miss was mine: I laid the start and nose, and the gap between them went unnoticed until about 4:45. I caught it, but that was later than it should have been.

**Execution:** My work was mostly connection checks and repairs. I found the start gap, the missing diagonal on the lower fin and the unconnected upper fin, and I fixed or flagged each one. Two things went less well. I swapped fin assignments with Jack, which cost a few rounds of confusion. I also spent time inspecting when I could have been laying dominoes. The loops in the middle were extra work we should not have done. I flagged them once I saw them, but the 45 spare dominoes show we over-planned.

**Collaboration:** I kept the table coordinated and asked people to say when their pieces joined. Sofia took the back half of the bottom line to meet Omar, and she did much of the junction cleanup. Omar and Jack covered the bottom body and upper fin. I told people to keep clear of the junction, which probably saved us from bumps there. I could have thanked and credited others earlier and more specifically.

**Leadership:** I set the plan, split the work and ran status checks. I also said plainly when something was broken, such as the start gap and the loops. I called the hands-off point once everything connected. The early fin mix-up and the late start-gap catch show I should have checked the basics sooner."}
